Free cholesterol transfers to HDL and is esteriﬁed by LCAT (which is activated by Apo A-1). Cholesteryl ester in the core of HDL
can be transferred to Apo B-containing particles, via CETP, in exchange for TG transfer to HDL. In this way, VLDL becomes smaller
and transforms to become IDL, although some small VLDLs may be removed directly. HL catabolizes TG in HDL resulting in the
formation of small HDL particles with the release and degradation of Apo A-1. HDL delivers cholesterol to the liver. Thereafter
a small HDL particle is released into the circulation.

Endogenous lipid pathway. Transport of TGs and cholesterol from sites of origin (liver) to peripheral tissues/organs.
The liver secretes
TG-rich, apo B-100 containing, nascent VLDL.
Apolipoproteins from HDL are transferred to nascent VLDL to form VLDL.
TGs and
cholesterol are delivered to peripheral tissues by VLDL decreasing the size which forms VLDL remnants.
Further lipolysis of VLDL remnants
forms IDL. IDL is either taken up by the liver or
is converted to LDL after removal of apo E and apo C.
